notes: Uniform Consumer-End Tariff: Under Section 31(7) of the Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997, the Federal Government notifies a uniform consumer-end tariff across all ex-WAPDA distribution companies (XWDISCOs), including LESCO, IESCO, and FESCO. S.R.O. 279(I)/2026 dated 12-02-2026 is the overarching uniform notification.

Protected Consumer Eligibility: Domestic consumers who consume 200 units or less per month consistently for the previous consecutive six (6) months qualify as Protected. If consumption exceeds 200 units in any single month, the consumer is classified as Unprotected for that month.
Benefit of One Previous Slab: Protected residential consumers are eligible for the incremental benefit of one previous slab rate under NEPRA guidelines.

Fixed Charges Shift: Starting from the February 2026 tariff rationalization decision (notified in S.R.O. 279(I)/2026), fixed charges for non-lifeline residential consumers were restructured onto a per kW sanctioned load basis (Rs. 200 to Rs. 675/kW/month), moving from purely per-consumer volumetric models to fixed cost recovery.

Time of Use (ToU) Billing: Residential connections with sanctioned load >= 5 kW are mandatorily on ToU meters with separate Peak and Off-Peak rates. Fixed charges of Rs. 675/kW/month are applied to 50% of the sanctioned load or actual recorded MDI, whichever is higher.

Taxes & Levies Sequencing: Electricity bills are computed by applying: (1) Base Energy Charges (slab-based) + (2) Fixed Capacity Charges + (3) Fuel Charges Adjustment (FCA) + (4) Quarterly Tariff Adjustment (QTA) + (5) Financing Cost Surcharge = Electricity Cost. GST (18%) is levied on this combined electricity cost. Provincial Electricity Duty (1.5%) is levied on energy charges. PTV Fee (Rs. 35) is added flat. For non-filers with gross bill >= Rs. 25,000, 7.5% advance income tax is collected.
